description_en: The three-bayed Bhailaḥ Phalcā, located at Kvaylāchi Ṭola, used to play an important role during Indrajatra and Buṅgadyaḥjātrā. Thephalcāhas an arcaded ground floor, a half upper floor and is connected to a private house. Its original structure is well preserved and an inscription dates the baluster columns back to 1871 CE. Minor renovations were undertaken in August of 2003 CE (VS 2060-65).
description_ne: तीन वटा कवल र पाँच वटा काष्ठस्तम्भ भएको यो फल्चाको भित्तामा टाँसिएको शिलालेखमा दिइएको जानकारी अनुसार यो फल्चा नेसं ९९१ (सन् १८७१) मा बनेको हो ।
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)

historical_events.event_description: A stone inscription is attached to the eastern wall of the Bhailaḥ Phalcā which provides information about its construction in 1871 CE (NS 991). According to the inscription, thephalcāwas built by Rāma Prajāpati Thakura and his family in the name of his late parents. Aguṭhīwas established at the same time, and land was donated to fund the organisation of annual rituals. As of 2018, theguṭhīno longer exists. Some of the rituals have therefore also come to an end.One can find images of the donors at the bottom of the inscription and a Bhairava flanked by two deities above it. Bhairava is shown standing in theālīḍhaposture with four arms; holding akhaḍgaand akhaṭvāṁka in his upper two hands.
